q: What are the emissions from drying ETP sludge before disposal?
title: Sludge drying: fuel and emissions
short: A thermal sludge dryer burns fuel or uses steam to drive off water, which is Scope 1. Drying cuts the weight you pay to transport and dispose of, which lowers Scope 3 waste emissions. Weigh both: fuel per tonne of water removed against tonnes no longer hauled.
audience: Textile, chemical and food plants with an ETP

ul: Fuel or steam for the dryer (Scope 1).
Transport and disposal of dried sludge (Scope 3, Category 5).
Solar drying beds where land allows.
Using waste heat from a boiler or kiln exhaust.
Better dewatering (filter press, centrifuge) before any thermal step.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.

sources.label: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
